description: Milestone 2.5 fixed evaluation set (ADR 0011). Cases are drawn from the real 100-issue pallets/flask demo fixture and, where a real GitHub issue number is referenced, use a bounded excerpt of that issue's real title/body -- never invented content. Deterministic expectations (classification/severity/action) were measured by running the real, unmodified app.triage.rules functions against the real issue text, not guessed. Retrieval semantic quality (similarity scores, hit rate) is intentionally NOT re-measured here -- see tests/calibration/bge_similarity_calibration.json for the frozen, real-BGE-model evidence this fixture's citation-wiring cases are grounded in.

cases.rationale: The primary Milestone 2.3 false-positive-correction case. Real, live-measured retrieval evidence (see calibration fixture): #5756 (0.928, confirmed near-duplicate) and #5863 (0.708, accepted via shared discriminative term 'security') are exactly what Jesse's own visible demo returned for this issue; #5942 (0.740, an unrelated packaging request) and #5804 (0.696, an unrelated request-lifecycle bug) were both real false positives caught and fixed during Milestone 2.3 and must never be re-introduced. This case proves the end-to-end wiring (supplied retrieval -> AI narrative citations -> citation validation) still honors exactly this known-correct, previously-measured outcome.
cases.title: Flask cannot find /security/logic API
cases.body: We are using airflow 2.8.4, and recently we upgrade it to 2.10.5. Environment: Python version 3.10, Flask version 2.2.5. Call /security/logic API and receive a 404 despite the route appearing to be registered correctly.
cases.expected_action: Escalate for security review before any further action.

cases.rationale: The near-duplicate target of sec_5755_primary. Confirms the classification rule is symmetric -- both halves of a real confirmed near-duplicate pair classify identically, which is what makes them a meaningful duplicate pair in the first place, not a coincidence of one case's wording.

cases.rationale: A second, independent real security-concern issue (a weak cryptographic default, not a duplicate of #5755/#5756), to prove the security-keyword rule generalizes rather than being tuned to one instance -- directly guards against the overfitting risk this project's own Milestone 2.5 readiness review flagged.
cases.title: [Security] Default session HMAC digest should be SHA-256, not SHA-1
cases.body: The session cookie signing implementation currently defaults to SHA-1 for the HMAC digest algorithm. SHA-1 is deprecated for cryptographic use and should default to SHA-256 instead.
cases.expected_action: Escalate for security review before any further action.

cases.rationale: A real bug-crash issue whose trigger keyword ('exception'/'traceback') is in the body, not the title -- proves the classifier reads the full issue text, not just the title, and that this fixture's bounded body excerpts are faithful enough to reproduce that.
cases.title: `stream_with_context` does not work with async routes
cases.body: When streaming a response with stream_with_context on an async route, the debugging middleware caught an exception in the streamed response at a point where response headers were already sent, followed by a traceback (most recent call last) during request handling.
cases.expected_action: Prioritize for immediate triage and request reproduction steps.

cases.rationale: The real issue behind sec_5755_primary's second forbidden citation. Its own title literally contains the word 'regression', but it classifies as bug-crash, not regression, because the crash-keyword rule is checked first and the body also contains 'exception'/'traceback' -- this documents the real rule-priority behavior (first match wins by rule order, not by text position) using a real, previously-established example rather than a synthetic one.
cases.title: 3.1.2 regression: `stream_with_context` triggers `teardown_request()` calls before response generation
cases.body: The teardown_request() callables are invoked too early, before response generation. The debugging middleware caught an exception in the streamed response at a point where response headers were already sent, producing a traceback during request handling.
cases.expected_action: Prioritize for immediate triage and request reproduction steps.

cases.rationale: A real documentation/support-request issue with the keyword in the title -- the plain, common case this rule exists for.
cases.title: Flask documentation website does not support dark mode
cases.body: The Flask documentation website does not offer a dark mode option, making it hard to read in low-light environments. Most modern documentation sites support this.
cases.expected_action: Route to documentation maintainers for a low-risk update.

cases.rationale: A second, independent real documentation issue -- guards against overfitting the rule to one wording.
cases.title: Inaccurate documentation for adding a favicon redirect
cases.body: The code sample in the existing documentation on how to redirect a favicon request assumes that add_url_rule takes a parameter named redirect_to. It does not.
cases.expected_action: Route to documentation maintainers for a low-risk update.

cases.rationale: Classifies as 'enhancement' only because the body happens to contain the word 'request' (from 'test request', not a feature request) -- a real, honest example of the deterministic keyword ruleset's known coarseness. Also the real issue used as an issue<->document calibration example in Milestone 2.3, giving this fixture and the retrieval calibration fixture a shared, cross-referenced real example.
cases.title: Session is not updated on redirect target endpoint in tests
cases.body: When using the test client to make a direct request to an endpoint after a redirect, the session values printed after the request do not reflect updates made during the redirect chain.
cases.expected_action: Queue as a candidate enhancement for roadmap review.

cases.rationale: A deliberately kept, honest example of a real deterministic-ruleset limitation: this issue reads like a bug report (a configuration setting being silently ignored) but classifies as 'enhancement' purely because 'request' appears in the body (from 'the underlying Werkzeug request object', not an enhancement request). This case exists to keep that known rough edge visible in every report -- a future ruleset change should not silently make this better or worse without deliberate review.
cases.title: MAX_FORM_MEMORY_SIZE not being picked up correctly
cases.body: Setting MAX_FORM_MEMORY_SIZE has no effect; the default 500000 bytes from the underlying Werkzeug request object is still used regardless of configuration.
cases.expected_action: Queue as a candidate enhancement for roadmap review.

cases.rationale: The exact real issue Jesse's Milestone 2.4 visible ownership check ran live triage against. No keyword rule matches; the fallback-to-closed-state rule applies. Also asserts the human-review boundary: the deterministic workflow must never auto-create a decision or leave anything but 'proposed'/'awaiting_human_review'.
cases.title: Admin endpoint seems to be reserved
cases.body: The admin route fails when the page argument is 1, 2, 3, or 8, using the default value instead of the actual argument. Replacing the route name from 'admin' to something else makes it work as expected.
cases.expected_action: Verify the closure is still valid before archiving.

cases.rationale: The only non-duplicate real example of the 'regression' label in the current 100-issue corpus -- the other four issues matching this rule (#6000-#6002, #6119) are exact duplicates or synthetic filler content, not genuine independent regression reports. That corpus-composition gap is itself an honest finding worth tracking (a future, more diverse issue corpus should add a second, genuinely distinct regression example) rather than padding this fixture with a near-duplicate or a weak example just to reach a round count.
cases.title: Missing tests: 9 source files have no test coverage
cases.body: This creates a gap in coverage and increases regression risk. 53 test files were found. Affected paths include several core modules without direct test coverage.
cases.expected_action: Flag as a regression and request the last known good version.

cases.rationale: The real punctuation-only issue already established in Milestone 2.3's calibration work as the canonical insufficient-query example: title and body both reduce to '.'. Proves the query-sufficiency gate (has_sufficient_query_content) correctly rejects it deterministically, with no embedding call or database query -- reusing the exact production functions, not a re-implementation.
cases.expected_action: Verify the closure is still valid before archiving.

cases.rationale: The real, minimal 'Tt' issue already established in Milestone 2.3's frozen calibration fixture (short_meaningful_query_examples): its query text IS meaningful enough to pass the sufficiency gate, but its real, measured similarity scores against the demo corpus (0.3673 and 0.4765) are well below the calibrated 0.65 threshold -- this case checks the query-sufficiency gate only (query IS sufficient) and cross-references the frozen calibration evidence for why real retrieval would still, correctly, return no qualifying evidence; it does not re-run retrieval to re-derive that fact.

cases.rationale: Exercises the real router/openai_adapter fallback path end-to-end, deterministically and offline: httpx.post is monkeypatched to raise a timeout before any request would be sent (never real network), proving the workflow still completes with a valid, zero-cost mock narrative and a recorded fallback_reason when the real provider is unreachable -- the safety property Milestone 2.2 built and Milestone 2.5 must keep proving, not just unit-test in isolation.

cases.rationale: Exercises citation validation end-to-end, deterministically and offline: a simulated OpenAI response claims an identifier ('issue:99999-invented') that was never supplied as retrieved context. The router must treat this exactly like any other controlled provider failure and fall back to the mock adapter -- proving an invented citation can never reach the persisted result.
cases.title: Flask cannot find /security/logic API
cases.body: We are using airflow 2.8.4, and recently we upgrade it to 2.10.5.

cases.rationale: A stronger, distinct edge case beyond a purely-invented citation: a simulated OpenAI response cites one genuinely-supplied identifier AND one invented one together -- proving citation validation is all-or-nothing per response (any invalid identifier rejects the whole set), a plausible real failure mode for an actual model response, not just the simplest possible invented-citation case.
cases.title: Modern CSRF Protection Using `Sec-Fetch-Site` Header
cases.body: Flask's security documentation states that CSRF protection requires a form validation framework, which Flask does not provide, necessitating one-time tokens. Modern browsers now support Sec-Fetch-Site headers, making token-based CSRF protection potentially unnecessary.

cases.rationale: The real, disclosed Milestone 2.3 polysemy limitation: #6139 (a demo-corpus filler issue genuinely discussing security vulnerabilities) was accepted as retrieval evidence for #5755 via the shared discriminative term 'security' -- a different sense of 'security' than #5755's URL-path name. This case deliberately does NOT assert any required or forbidden citation relationship between #5755 and #6139 -- doing so would either reward a known-imperfect behavior or falsely demand a fix this milestone does not deliver. It exists only to keep this limitation visible in every future report, per Jesse's explicit correction.

cases.title: flask run should support pep723
cases.body: Because no one wants to use native pkgutil-style packaging, setup.py, setup.cfg, pyproject.toml, pep517, setuptools, build, or pip for a simple script. Having flask run support inline PEP 723 dependencies would simplify running a Flask application significantly.
cases.expected_action: Verify the closure is still valid before archiving.
